summary.headline: Alicon Q2 FY27 total income hit a record Rs 652 crore (+50% YoY), with EBITDA up 14% YoY to Rs 65.3 crore and margin at 10%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was a record Rs 652 crore, up 50.4% YoY and 12.6% QoQ, with alloy-adjusted revenue growth of 24% YoY. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% YoY to Rs 65.3 crore, but margin of 10% (12.1% alloy-adjusted) was held back by commodity and cost inflation. PAT grew 27% YoY to Rs 17.6 crore and H1 PAT rose 25% to Rs 29.1 crore. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 12-15% alloy-adjusted growth, while signalling a likely upward revision to revenue guidance, and flagged Q3 seasonal softness with Q4 expected to be stronger.

segments.name: Domestic automotive
segments.commentary: Q2 alloy-adjusted revenue growth of 24% YoY versus market growth of around 19%; tonnage up 19.3% YoY and 15% QoQ. Two-wheelers about 40% of revenue, passenger vehicles 36-38%, commercial vehicles about 18%.

segments.name: Europe (Slovakia)
segments.commentary: Sequential revenue growth in Q2 after mature programs ended; global share about 13% of revenue. Management expects exports to reach 18-20% of revenue by end FY27.

segments.name: Non-auto
segments.commentary: Share of revenue in the residual category per management; data-centre sales guided at Rs 3-4 crore in FY27 and Rs 15-20 crore next year; tractor segment guided at Rs 12-15 crore a year from next year.

segments.name: Illichmann Castalloy (Europe subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making; break-even estimated at about Rs 30-40 crore quarterly sales. Management expects EBITDA positive next year (FY28).

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated at 12-15% alloy-adjusted revenue growth; management said it expects to revise revenue guidance upward and that alloy-adjusted growth could be around 15% or more.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected around 12% (alloy-adjusted), with at least 1% YoY margin improvement thereafter; management targets 14-15% by FY30.
Tonnage growth of around 15% plus expected for FY27 overall, with Q3 seasonally soft and Q4 strong.
Capex for FY27 about Rs 150 crore against Rs 70 crore in H1 (including Rs 40 crore of leased assets); funded mainly by internal accruals.
Pune plant (12,000 MT capacity, about Rs 125-130 crore investment) expected to enter mass manufacturing by April 2027; first-year revenue guided at Rs 120-150 crore.
Aluminium prices expected to fall about 20-25% from September to December levels; management says 100% of raw-material inflation passed through in H1.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 50,000 tonnes per year, utilisation 82-84%; management says about 20% headroom is ideal.
New Pune plant adds 12,000 metric tonnes per year; asset turnover guided at 3.5-4x and up to 3x at peak utilisation; capacity reportedly fully booked by customers.
H1 FY27 capex about Rs 70 crore including Rs 40 crore leased; full-year plan about Rs 150 crore including Pune phase-wise investment.
Further capacity expansion and strategic investments under evaluation; no approvals announced yet.
demand_pricing: Executable order book about Rs 6,700 crore as of 30 Sep 2026, covering FY27 through FY31-32.
Q2 added eight parts from three customers: about 95% passenger vehicle and 5% non-auto; peak annual sales about Rs 270 crore, around Rs 1,000 crore over six years; around 70% of volumes from FY28-29.
Cylinder head market share in Indian CV rose from about 13% in FY26 to 23% in H1 FY27; estimated two-wheeler share 30-35%, passenger vehicle 14-18%, CV 13-15%.
Around 25-30 new part numbers to start SOP over the next year, including EV and global CV programs in Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 volume growth of 19%: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ramp-up of new CV developments, higher share of business with existing customers, and deemed exports from two Chennai-based customers shipping to Europe and US.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,950 crore be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is looking for a revision upward; Q3 is typically soft and Q4 strong. Alloy-adjusted growth target is 12-15%, currently seen around 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margin about 12% alloy-adjusted; at least 1% YoY improvement after that, supporting 14-15% by FY30 per CFO, which management described as a striving goal.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and inventory build, weaker cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to aluminium price jump and volume growth; customers are slow to approve payments, with collections expected in the next two to three months. Management said this is a timing issue, not margin.

qa_highlights.question: Slovakia and Illichmann viability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Slovakia is strategic for niche high-technology parts; Illichmann needs Rs 30-40 crore quarterly sales to break even and should turn EBITDA positive in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Pune plant asset turnover and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset turnover guided at 3x at peak (3.5-4x per later comment) with roughly Rs 500 crore revenue over four to five years on Rs 125-130 crore investment. ROCE of 15% described as a valid, doable goal, with no date given.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivables rose about Rs 88 crore and inventory about Rs 32 crore in the quarter, weighing on cash conversion; collection timing depends on customer approvals.
Input costs: aluminium expected to ease, but other commodity, energy, and labour inflation (including European cost pressures) remain; alloy-adjusted margin 12.1% versus reported 10%.
Europe: Slovakia and Illichmann still loss-making; recovery described as gradual and dependent on new programs; exports fell sharply in the period.
Capacity: utilisation at 82-84% against a 50,000 tonne base; the Pune plant timeline (April 2027) and new-customer SOPs are key execution items.
Management declined to quantify post-FY30 revenue ambition or inorganic opportunities; both to be shared later.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order wins and top-line momentum, but cautious on margins, Europe and the near-term outlook; management repeatedly avoided specific long-term numbers and deferred inorganic and beyond-FY30 targets.
key_quotes: We are looking for a revision to this for sure.
We will never take any target which is an average target to be taken by any company.
As of now, we do not see any significant challenge to us.

financial_highlights.change: Net debt to annualised H1 EBITDA 1.33x

adds.what: 12,000 MT/yr Pune plant (about Rs 125-130 crore investment), entering mass manufacturing by April 2027

growth.why: FY27 alloy-adjusted revenue growth guidance of 12-15% reiterated (management signals upward revision toward 15%+), backed by 83% utilisation of 50,000 tpa, the 12,000 MT Pune plant due April 2027 (fully booked per management), and an executable order book of about Rs 6,700 crore.

oneOffs.what: Alloy price pass-through inflated reported revenue: total income +50.4% YoY vs +24% alloy-adjusted growth

quality.why: Reported total income grew 50.4% YoY, but about 26 points of that gap is alloy price pass-through rather than volume, leaving 24% alloy-adjusted growth; tonnage grew 19.3% YoY, so volume and new CV ramp-up are the real recurring drivers, with the Chennai deemed-export contribution not sized.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 alloy-adjusted EBITDA margin guided around 12% (Q2 alloy-adjusted 12.1%, reported 10%), with at least 1% YoY improvement thereafter toward 14-15% by FY30, though management called the FY30 goal a striving target.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 12,000 MT/yr Pune plant (about Rs 125-130 crore) is under construction with mass manufacturing committed by April 2027, adding 24% to the 50,000 tpa base.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Tonnage guided at around 15%+ for FY27, Q2 tonnage up 19.3% YoY, and utilisation at 82-84% with the order book at about Rs 6,700 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 82-84% against the 50,000 tpa base, and further expansion is under evaluation with no approvals yet, but the Pune plant already covers near-term needs.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is looking to revise FY27 revenue guidance (Rs 1,950 crore) upward, with alloy-adjusted growth seen around 15% or more versus the 12-15% range, and H1 total income up 44% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance is being reiterated and raised, with the order book at about Rs 6,700 crore and Q2 alloy-adjusted revenue up 24% YoY; the risks are a soft Q3 and input-cost inflation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 25-30 new part numbers to start SOP over the next year including EV and global CV programs, and data-centre sales (Rs 3-4 crore in FY27, Rs 15-20 crore next year) plus tractor parts (Rs 12-15 crore a year from next year).

rows.label: Illichmann Castalloy EBITDA positive
rows.why: Still loss-making; management expects EBITDA positive next year, with break-even at about Rs 30-40 crore quarterly sales.

rows.label: Receivables and inventory unwind
rows.why: Receivables rose about Rs 88 crore and inventory about Rs 32 crore in Q2 (34 working-capital days), with collections expected in two to three months as aluminium prices fall 20-25%.

rows.label: Europe export share to 18-20%
rows.why: Exports are guided to reach 18-20% of revenue by end FY27 from a Europe/Slovakia share of about 13%, though exports fell sharply in the period.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book, and top-line momentum (Pune plant fully booked), but cautious on margins, Europe, and cash conversion; analysts pressed on the receivables build, Illichmann viability, and deferred FY30 and post-FY30 targets.
